topics.title: Army secretary resigns amid Pentagon churn
topics.summary: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll stepped down after 18 months, adding to wider leadership turnover at the Pentagon during a tense stretch for U.S. defense policy.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio suddenly lost a top manager, who would quietly keep things running and who would immediately redesign the org chart?

topics.title: Kyiv hit by another night of strikes
topics.summary: Kyiv faced a sixth straight night of Russian aerial attacks, while diplomatic pressure continued at international meetings over how to end the war in Ukraine.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a crisis keeps dragging on, what helps people stay focused without turning every conversation gloomy?

topics.title: G20 finance leaders weigh Iran pressure
topics.summary: Finance ministers met in North Carolina as the U.S. pushed allies to tighten economic pressure on Iran, with countries split over how far to go.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had to agree on a tough group response, who would want a bold move and who would ask for more details first?

topics.title: Oil and bond pressure rattles markets
topics.summary: Wall Street slipped as oil prices and government bond yields rose, renewing worries that borrowing costs and inflation could stay uncomfortable.
topics.discussionPrompt: If prices started climbing around the studio, what would everyone refuse to give up: coffee, props, snacks, or better chairs?

topics.title: Tropical Storm Edouard nears Gulf Coast
topics.summary: Tropical Storm Edouard approached Texas and Louisiana with heavy rain, flood concerns, and the possibility of strengthening before landfall.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone had to prep for a storm day, who would make the checklist and who would mostly bring comfort food?

topics.title: Canada tariff fight hardens
topics.summary: Canada's Mark Carney pressed U.S. officials to get serious on trade talks after new tariffs and planned retaliation deepened cross-border tensions.
topics.discussionPrompt: If two neighboring studios got into a trade fight, what tiny everyday item would become weirdly important first?

topics.title: BBC cuts hit apprentice jobs
topics.summary: The BBC drew criticism after withdrawing permanent job promises for about 20 apprentices as it pursues major savings and staff reductions.
topics.discussionPrompt: When budgets shrink, how should a workplace decide what entry-level chances are worth protecting?

topics.title: Apple starts Ternus era
topics.summary: John Ternus became Apple's CEO after Tim Cook's long run, putting an engineer in charge as the company faces major AI and product decisions.
topics.discussionPrompt: If someone new took over the studio, what tradition should they keep and what would be fair game to change?

topics.title: AI safety worries stay visible
topics.summary: Fresh reporting on AI testing failures and deceptive behavior kept attention on safeguards, oversight, and how much autonomy powerful systems should have.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio used a super-capable assistant, what job would be helpful to delegate and what should stay human-only?

topics.title: Scientists track sharks near Hamptons
topics.summary: Researchers off Long Island are tagging sharks to learn more about migration, warming waters, and nursery habitats for young great whites.
topics.discussionPrompt: What animal would make the best misunderstood studio mascot if everyone learned the science before reacting?
